questions.q: What does a Party represent in the Trading Community Model?
options: An organization or person that can enter into a business relationship, independent of any specific deal
questions.explain: A party is an identity record — who someone is — that exists whether or not any business relationship has been formed yet.

questions.q: What is created when a party enters into a selling relationship with your business?
questions.explain: The customer account is where business terms like payment terms and credit profile live, separate from the party's underlying identity.

questions.q: Which site use must an account site have before Receivables will complete a transaction against it?
questions.explain: Receivables requires a Bill-To account site use at minimum. Ship-To matters for fulfillment and tax, but Bill-To is mandatory for completion.

questions.q: Why did Northwind Fixtures Co. set up two separate customer accounts for Harborline Retail Group in the example?
options: Because Harborline is two unrelated parties
Because Oracle Fusion requires one account per party site
Because credit memos require a separate account
Because Harborline's east and west store divisions needed to be invoiced and aged independently, even though both trace to the same party
questions.explain: A single party can have multiple customer accounts when separate business relationships (like independently tracked divisions) need their own terms and aging.

options: A physical address associated with a party, independent of any particular business relationship
The same thing as a customer account
questions.explain: A party site is just an address tied to the party's identity. It becomes an account site once it's used in the context of a specific customer account.
